extracted.intended_audience: Boys & Girls Clubs staff, volunteers, supervisors, HR, and job candidates (Northwest San Diego)
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational personnel, safety, technology, incident, drug/alcohol, and transportation policies and procedures for staff, volunteers, and members at a youth-serving Club. Covers screening, onboarding, acceptable use, incident reporting/investigation, testing, and vehicle/transport rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-employment screening and drug-free workplace compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure new hires complete pre-employment steps (drug screening, background checks, fingerprinting) in accordance with the Drug-Free Workplace Policy prior to first day of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal is to provide a safe environment through a reliable process; organization may alter hiring practices at any time. Reference to Drug-Free Workplace Policy for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviewing process
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct in-person behavioral-based interviews with every candidate (may include multiple interview stages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavioral-based format; applies to employment and program volunteer service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference checks for direct-contact roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct reference checks on any candidate for employment or volunteer positions with direct repetitive contact with young people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If candidate previously worked at a Boys & Girls Club, obtain eligibility-for-rehire/volunteering information from all previous Clubs before extending an offer; BGCNWSD provides reference materials to other Member Organizations upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onboarding: employee handbook delivery and acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon offer, new employees must receive and confirm in writing receipt of an up-to-date employee policies and procedures manual or handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handbook must at minimum articulate current: Conditions of employment; Benefits; Rights and responsibilities of employees; Club safety policies; Any other important employment-related information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation content for new staff and volunteers
rubrics_metrics.description: Before working with Club members, staff and volunteers must receive an orientation covering organizational mission/goals/policies, job descriptions and performance standards, participant needs, personnel policies, operational procedures, and required Child Abuse Prevention Trainings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orientation topics include schedule, cultural/socioeconomic characteristics of participants, expectations regarding work hours/schedules, safety/supervision/transportation/facilities/emergency operations, and completion of BGCA-approved trainings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring process objective and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The hiring process must ensure new hires complete all required pre-employment steps to protect members' safety; the organization reserves the right to change hiring practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-employment steps explicitly include drug screening, background checks, and fingerprinting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug and Alcohol-Free Workplace commitment and legal compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a drug- and alcohol-free workplace and comply with the Federal Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 and California’s Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1990.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'illegal or unauthorized drugs' including marijuana (federal Schedule I), and distinguishes nonpsychoactive marijuana in California.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of illegal/unauthorized drugs and prescription misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Illegal/unauthorized drugs include illegal controlled substances (including marijuana under federal law) and prescription/OTC drugs being abused or used contrary to prescribed purpose/quantity/frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies legal vs illegal (e.g., nonpsychoactive marijuana legal for over-18 in CA is not in definition); includes misuse of prescribed or OTC meds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on working while under the influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees and volunteers are prohibited from reporting to work or working while under the influence of alcohol and/or illegal or unauthorized drugs and from using them on premises, at events, or while representing BGCNWSD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderated use of alcohol during approved BGCNWSD-sponsored events is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescription drug notification and accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee taking a legal drug that potentially affects job safety/performance must notify their supervisor, Chief HR Officer, and/or Club leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If healthcare provider and organization determine no adverse effect or a reasonable accommodation can be made, employee may work; if unable to perform essential functions even with accommodation, employee may need leave per healthcare provider's conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conviction reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees must notify supervisor/Club leadership/Chief Human Resources Officer within five (5) days of any conviction of a drug/alcohol-related crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BGCNWSD may impose corrective measures within 30 calendar days of notice, subject to law, including termination or requiring participation in approved drug abuse assistance or rehabilitation programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary self-reporting and reasonable accommodation for treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: If an employee voluntarily reports having an alcohol or drug problem prior to any policy violation, BGCNWSD will encourage treatment and reasonably accommodate participation in rehabilitation if it does not impose undue hardship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to encourage early help-seeking; accommodations depend on undue hardship analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary consequences and inspection rights for violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any employee or volunteer violating the Drug and Alcohol-Free Workplace Policy is subject to disciplinary action up to and including termination, even for a first offense. Organization may inspect organization-issued lockers, desks, or suspected concealment areas and personal property when reasonable suspicion exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization reserves all appropriate and lawful actions to enforce policy; inspections triggered by reasonable suspicion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-accident and reasonable-suspicion drug/alcohol testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization may require drug and alcohol testing post-accident when driving on BGCNWSD business resulting in serious injury, significant property damage, or arrest/citation; also may test when objective observable behaviors justify reasonable suspicion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees who delay accident notification may be disciplined. Reasonable-suspicion evidence examples follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective indicators for reasonable-suspicion testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence sufficient for reasonable suspicion may include alcohol on the breath, aberrant behavior, physical symptoms (slurred speech, bloodshot eyes), lapses in performance, and inability to appropriately respond to questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisors trained in identification must independently observe an employee’s actions before authorizing testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for refusing drug/alcohol testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees refusing to submit to any test under this policy will be subject to discipline up to and including immediate termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident management and mandatory reporting expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff and volunteers must immediately report and document all safety incidents that might affect staff, volunteers, members, and others who visit Clubhouses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting and documentation are essential elements for responding to incidents; incidents include a broad range of safety events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of safety incidents to report (general list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety incidents include but are not limited to: inappropriate adult-youth activity, inappropriate youth-youth activity, allegations of abuse, bullying, inappropriate electronic communications between adults and youth, minor/major medical emergencies, threats, physical assaults/injuries, missing children, criminal activity, and other incidents as deemed by leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incidents include those occurring during programs, on premises, or during Club-affiliated trips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal incident reporting content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone aware of an incident must immediately complete an incident report and submit it to Club leadership including date, location, witnesses and contact information, names of all involved (youth and staff), and all notifications made (first responders, parents, leadership, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide as much detail as applicable in the Incident Report section.

rubrics_metrics.name: External incident reporting and mandated reporting compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: BGCNWSD follows all mandated reporting statutes and applicable laws for protection/safety of youth; types of externally reportable incidents include inappropriate adult-youth activity, allegations of child abuse, child pornography, criminal activity, missing children, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow federal/state/local laws and licensing requirements; report to appropriate external agencies as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: BGCA critical incident reporting (24-hour requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Member Organizations must immediately report allegations of abuse or potential criminal matters to law enforcement and report specific critical incidents to BGCA within 24 hours (items A–K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of reportable items A–K includes child abuse by staff/volunteer, youth-on-youth abuse, missing/abducted child, major medical emergencies, abuse/harassment involving staff/volunteers/visitors, licensing noncompliance, suspected felony acts, misappropriation of funds ($10,000+ or any federal funds), legal actions, negative media attention, and any other incident deemed critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident investigation process and suspension protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: BGCNWSD supports external investigations and conducts internal Safety Committee investigations only when incidents are not externally reportable; compliance with criminal/child protective reporting laws must precede internal inquiries. If allegation involves staff/volunteer/member, the individual shall be suspended immediately (employees with pay) throughout investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal investigations are not a substitute for criminal or CPS investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology acceptable use: member agreement and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Members (and parents/guardians) must read and sign the Technology Acceptable Use policy before using Club technology or personal devices. Club devices and personally owned devices are defined broadly to include devices that capture media, transmit messages, or access content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Club purposes defined as program activities, career development, communication, homework, etc.; members expected to ask staff when unsure about permissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized and restricted device use for members
rubrics_metrics.description: Club and personally owned devices are permitted only during approved Club times for Club purposes and in approved locations; use in locker rooms, restrooms, and other privacy-expected areas is expressly prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized use can lead to confiscation, suspension, membership termination, or law enforcement referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate communications and prohibited content (members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members may not use technology to harass, threaten, demean, humiliate, intimidate, embarrass, or annoy others; prohibited communications include obscene/profane language/images, content that causes damage/disruption, personal attacks, harassment/stalking, knowingly posting false/defamatory information, or promoting destructive acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ordered to stop sending communications, member must cease immediately; violations subject to disciplinary action per Club policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and inspection of member devices
rubrics_metrics.description: BGCNWSD reserves the right to monitor, inspect, copy, and review personally owned devices brought to the Club; parents/guardians will be notified before inspection and may be present; parental refusal may bar future device bring-ins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspections are subject to parental notification/choice and may result in barring devices if parents refuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member responsibility for device loss and damage
rubrics_metrics.description: Members are responsible for keeping personal devices with them; staff are not responsible and Club is not liable for loss, damage, misuse, or theft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyberbullying prohibition and examples (members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyberbullying—using technology to harass/threaten/demean/humiliate/intimidate/embarrass others—is prohibited and subject to disciplinary action. Examples include harassing texts/emails/social media comments, rumors posted online, embarrassing pictures/videos, or fake profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any cyberbullying that disrupts safety or well-being of Club is actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unauthorized access and illegal online acts (members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members may not attempt unauthorized access to Club or other computer systems, use Club network to facilitate illegal acts (e.g., arrange purchase/sale of drugs), threaten safety, or deliberately disrupt systems or spread viruses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations may lead to disciplinary action or legal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet access restrictions for members
rubrics_metrics.description: Personally owned devices must use Club’s content-filtered wireless network and may not connect directly through phone networks or other providers; Club reserves right to monitor/manage access and open/close websites or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must follow Club procedures to access internet service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital citizenship and annual training (members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members must conduct themselves online in accordance with the Club Code of Conduct; online violations subject to the same discipline as offline; all members must complete BGCA-provided digital citizenship and technology safety training annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is required yearly before using Club devices/equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff and volunteer technology use agreement and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must read and sign the Technology Acceptable Use policy and the 'Unacceptable Use Policy' in the Employee Handbook before using Club technology or bringing personal devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff are expected to ask supervisors when unsure about permissibility of technology use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized and appropriate staff device use
rubrics_metrics.description: Personally owned devices are permitted for Club purposes only during approved times and locations; use in locker rooms/restrooms or other privacy-expected areas is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inappropriate use may lead to confiscation, suspension, termination, or law enforcement referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, inspection, and consequences for staff device refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: BGCNWSD reserves the right to monitor/inspect personally owned staff devices brought to the Club; staff may refuse such inspections but refusal may lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike member inspections, refusal by staff may have immediate employment consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate communication examples and prohibitions (staff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff prohibited from obscene/profane/lewd/vulgar/threatening sexual or disrespectful communications/images, information that causes conflict, personal attacks or discriminatory attacks, harassment/stalking, knowingly posting false/defamatory info, or promoting property destruction or weapons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff told to stop must cease immediately; violations subject to disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff cyberbullying prohibition and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff may not use technology to harass, threaten, demean, humiliate, intimidate, embarrass or annoy others—behavior defined as cyberbullying—and is subject to discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples mirror member examples: harassing messages, rumors, embarrassing media, fake profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff communication protocol with members
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff may never use personal devices to communicate directly with a single Club member; all communication between staff and Club members must include an additional staff member and at least two Club members (applies to overnight events and conferences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper protocol requires inclusion of other staff and members to avoid one-on-one electronic contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff device password and access security requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Devices must lock and require authentication using strongest available features; minimum standard is a typed password of at least six characters or numbers, though biometrics are acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement aims to prevent unauthorized access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited staff behaviors and media/materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Not allowed: sexually explicit/unprofessional material on computers/personal devices, unprofessional communications with staff or campers, communications using social media except via Club email with parent and director permission, creating/recording music videos or recordings (except when instructed), texting campers, sharing personal email/social media addresses with campers, sharing inappropriate 'adult' materials on Club premises, inappropriate personal photos in offices or on person, cell phone restrictions during camp hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Employee Handbook 'Unacceptable Use' for more detail; cell phones not permitted during camp hours unless pre-approved by supervisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation policy scope and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines transportation as active movement by any vehicle (Club-owned or personal) transporting youth; Clubs provide transport only to/from Clubhouses or organization-related activities; policy aims to maintain safe vehicles and personal safety of adults and youth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to members, staff, volunteers, and Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vehicle care, maintenance, and operator responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: When using BGCNWSD vehicles, employees must exercise care, perform required maintenance, follow operating instructions, safety standards and guidelines, and promptly report any damage/defect or repair needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt reporting prevents deterioration and ensures safety; regular maintenance records should be kept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for improper/unsafe vehicle use
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper, careless, negligent, destructive, or unsafe use or operation of vehicles, as well as excessive or avoidable traffic/parking violations, can result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on transporting members in personal vehicles
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff, volunteers, and Board members shall not transport Club members and program participants in personal vehicles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only official BGCNWSD vehicles are permitted for transporting members.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-on-one and minimum-occupancy transport rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not transport one member alone (one-on-one policy); ensure at least a total of two other individuals are present when transporting youth; in some driver-specific points, require at least three individuals present—if one child remains to be dropped off, two adults (18+) must be present in vehicle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to prevent one-on-one unsupervised situations and increase safety and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Driver documentation and pre-trip checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Drivers must follow vehicle pre-inspection guidelines, complete required transportation documents, keep logs of youth picked-up and dropped-off, perform regular checks so no youth are left unattended, and sign a daily log confirming seat-by-seat scans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accurate logs and perform visual checks after every trip; submit written incident reports for issues/accidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and reporting responsibilities for transport issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Drivers must immediately notify Club Supervisors/Managers if delays or issues occur transporting members and must submit written incident reports detailing any issues or accidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows timely response to transport issues and proper documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Driver background clearance and barrier crime policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Drivers must allow DMV background checks and be cleared to transport youth per the organization's barrier crime policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearance is mandatory before transporting youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport safety checks and vehicle condition reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform regular checks to ensure proper pick-up/drop-off, that no members are left unattended, inspect and ensure seat belts working, implement/report systems for vehicle conditions and maintenance, keep vehicles clean, and inspect vehicles per DMV/local/state/federal requirements before trips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow DMV inspection guidance and maintain documentation of maintenance/inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seat belt and regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each vehicle must provide a seat belt for every passenger and fully comply with state and federal seat belt regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimizing mixed-age transport and passenger behavior management
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimize transport of mixed age groups (children, teens, adults) when possible; monitor passenger behaviors when vehicle is idle or parked; don't leave passengers unattended; prohibit audio devices at loud/distracting levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document disruptive passenger behaviors (excessive noise, refusal to wear seatbelts) and address safety concerns; conduct visual inspections to ensure no youth left in vehicles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for transportation and vehicle use
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide transportation and vehicle use policy and procedures training for staff during new hire training and throughout the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing training reinforces safety protocols and compliance.
